Current-base refresh: approved checkout d65ab43c22f297d656baadc8411a1a501636d5c2. Reuse the previously reviewed design after delivered PRs; no implementation has begun. The coordinator verified both proposed new paths absent at this base.

# ISSUE-334 plan

Separate repository PR feedback from comprehensive nightly/release validation using existing workflows and tests. Change only CI, this repository's trusted policy, and explanatory documentation. The approved sensitive profile and agent review gate remain in force; independent review must check the trust and release boundaries.

## Dimensions

Risk is approved as sensitive. Advisory size: multi-area; uncertainty: medium. Expected effort fits the 16-hour claim budget. No execution profile changes.

## What we know

- `.github/workflows/swarm-validate.yml:1` admits PRs, main pushes, reusable calls and manual dispatch. Its test-matrix job runs full race tests and six cross-builds; its policy job independently runs trusted required checks (`:163`, `:195`). This duplicates work.
- `.swarm/validation/required-checks.yaml:1` contains formatting, build, vet, staticcheck and full non-race tests; `:17` starts protected paths. Preserve the complete protected-path list.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml:16` calls CI; snapshot and publish require checks and eligibility. `.goreleaser.yaml:5` defines Linux/macOS/Windows on amd64/arm64.
- Existing tests enforce trusted merge-parent policy, grant isolation, workflow-copy security steps and reusable-call permissions: `internal/harness/scaffold_test.go:784,1017,1042,1091`, `internal/harness/workflow_permissions_test.go:140`; candidate-policy tampering is covered by `internal/validation/validator_test.go:99`.
- Existing changed-package fast pass still runs the full suite and is disabled in CI (`internal/validation/validator.go:264`, `internal/validation/go_fastpass_test.go:140,226`). It cannot supply this PR lane without runtime changes; preserve it unchanged.
- Checks use `cleanCheckEnv` (`internal/validation/validator.go:561`), native snapshots omit `.git` (`internal/sandbox/worker.go:682`), and warm-up executes trusted commands on the base (`internal/validation/build_cache.go:66`). Fixed commands work without selection context.
- Repository search found no Go Benchmark functions or benchmark/performance target. Record this gap; add no benchmark suite or experiments.
- `/swarm-plan` is the artifact-writing procedure in `.claude/commands/swarm-plan.md:1`; publication and claim mutation remain coordinator responsibilities.

## What we're assuming

The snapshot matches the approved checkout. Git metadata is unavailable here (`git rev-parse HEAD` failed), so the coordinator/developer must verify approved-base identity and path existence before implementation. The operator reports current root HTTPS transport working; transport work is out of scope.

## Open questions

- New file paths below are absent in this snapshot but cannot be confirmed absent at the approved base here. Verify with `git cat-file -e "$BASE_SHA:<path>"` before creation; if present, treat as modifications and inspect first.
- Hosted schedule execution, branch protection check names and actual release admission require maintainer/CI inspection. Offline workflow inspection supplies acceptance evidence without blocking implementation on hosted access. Preserve current required job names where practical; document any required branch-protection adjustment.

## Implementation sequence and exact touchpoints

1. Modify `.swarm/validation/required-checks.yaml` required_checks only. Retain fmt/build/vet/staticcheck over all source. Replace the full test command with the fixed commands below, unconditionally in every environment: CI repo validation, coordinator/local isolated-native issue/PR validation, and approved-base cache warm-up. No changed-area selection, Git commands, base/environment dependency, candidate helper, framework, new flags or runtime changes in policy commands. Policy loading still uses the approved trusted base and fails closed on authority errors; commands themselves need no base. Keep finite check budgets covering the listed Go timeouts. This fixes only blocking F1.

Mandatory security/smoke commands, once on every PR (including docs-only):

```bash
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/cli -run '^Test(CLIRepoValidateHarnessGrantNeedsAuthoritativeState|RepoValidateGrantOnlyRunsNoChecks|RepoValidateGrantFileRechecked|RootDefaultEnvironment|RootInjectedEnvironment|ResolveBuildVersion|ResolveBuildVersionWithoutVCS)$' -count=1
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/gitcredential/... ./internal/safefs/... -count=1
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/agent -run '^Test(DefaultModeNeverRunsHostAgent|OperatorCannotWeakenApprovedIsolation|MockCannotBypassIsolation|IsolatedRunnerRejectsHostCredentialsAndUnrestrictedNetwork|NativeCodexRejectsPolicyOverrides|NativeIsolatedEffortAdmitsNoOtherArguments|IsolatedBackendIsExplicit|ConfiguredRunnerRejectsPublishingCredentialForwarding|RestrictedEnvRemovesPublishingCredentials|ConfiguredRunnerWithLookupRejectsCredentialNames|AdapterProcessHidesPublishingCredentials)$' -count=1
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/sandbox -run '^Test(WorkerArchiveRoundTripAndImport|WorkerImportRejectsConcurrentChanges|WorkerRejectsHostileArchives|WorkerInputRejectsLinksAndCancellation|WorkerRejectsUnpinnedImageAndDoesNotForwardCredentials|WorkerInputRejectsPortableAliases|WorkerEmptyEnvironmentNeverInherits|WorkerOCIMissingCapabilitiesFailClosed|DependencyCacheNoFallback|NativeCodexBoundary|ToolExecutorBoundary)$' -count=1
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/fork -run '^Test(GatewayDeadlineCancelsInFlightScan|GatewayIgnoresMismatchedOrEditedResults|ForkJSONRejectsTrailingMalformedData|ForkCoordinatorSecurityAndLifecycle|OperationListsStayInSync|ForkRequestRejectsCarryAuthority)$' -count=1
```

The fixed core regression commands also run in every environment:

```bash
go test -timeout=10m ./internal/validation/... ./internal/harness/... ./internal/coordination/... ./internal/lease/... ./internal/contract/...
go test -timeout=5m ./cmd/changelog ./internal/changelog
```

The core command owns harness/validation regressions exactly once; named CLI and security commands own their listed regressions. These packages plus the mandatory named commands are the entire fixed PR test profile, for ordinary, CLI, protected/security, broad, unknown and docs-only changes alike. Broad changes use the same fixed profile; full behavior coverage, including the entire CLI package, runs nightly/release. No conditional fallback or full-repository test command is part of PR policy. Retain `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go tool staticcheck ./...` and formatting over all source.

2. Modify `.github/workflows/swarm-validate.yml` jobs, preserving trusted validator construction, grant verification steps, token scoping, protected-path modes and exact checked-out revision. Keep policy validation as the single owner of required fmt/build/static/test checks; remove equivalent unconditional lint/test-matrix runs. Retain CLI build/smoke and changelog validation once, without race or distribution campaigns. Preserve applicable existing security.yml scans; do not modify fork-coordinator or scaffold templates. Preserve the existing trusted-base resolution for policy/grant enforcement; export no base to check commands. PR events contain no repository-wide tests, `-race`, GOOS loop, benchmarks or call to `full-validation.yml` (F4).
3. Add `.github/workflows/full-validation.yml` as one reusable workflow with `workflow_call`, nightly `schedule`, and `workflow_dispatch` (no separate nightly wrapper needed). Reuse current Ubuntu 26.04/bubblewrap setup, pinned actions, identity setup and finite budgets. Run full `go test -timeout=15m ./...` and `go test -race -timeout=15m ./...`, formatting/static/vulnerability checks, CLI smoke, changelog check and all six existing cross-builds. Preserve existing test assertions and distribution support. Record the missing benchmark target in summary/docs. Retain test/build logs and resolved commit in bounded-retention artifacts with failure uploads and summaries; preserve command failures through pipes. Use read-only permissions and no inherited release secrets.
4. Modify `.github/workflows/release.yml:16` checks to call the full reusable workflow. Both snapshot and publish must require its success and existing eligibility, without `always()`/continue-on-error bypasses. Resolve the release event commit once and use that immutable SHA in validation, eligibility and packaging checkouts, checking HEAD matches it. Never reuse a green nightly run for a different SHA. Preserve release-only write credentials, environment gate, attestation and tag/default-branch checks. Avoid shared concurrency groups that cancel a release's called validation.
5. Modify `docs/developer.md` to explain the fixed PR profile for all changes, mandatory security regressions, and full behavior coverage (including the entire CLI package) nightly/release, bootstrap behavior, nightly/manual invocation, results and release gate. Update the CI comparison sentence in `README.md:81` and Makefile's `check` comment (`Makefile:50`) to describe full local/nightly checks accurately; keep target behavior unchanged. Add one `changes/unreleased/334.md` bullet. No product runtime, external scaffold, new tests, new issues, benchmarks or performance experiments.

Bootstrap: this PR must run every check from its old approved base, including its full test command. Candidate YAML does not override it. The fast policy takes effect only after merging into a trusted base. Do not disable validation or modify claim policy to accelerate this first run.

## HANDOFF

- Entry points: CI jobs `.github/workflows/swarm-validate.yml:18,111`; policy `.swarm/validation/required-checks.yaml:1`; release checks/needs `.github/workflows/release.yml:16,45,67`; distribution list `.goreleaser.yaml:5` (preserve). The full workflow and changelog fragment are absent in this snapshot; approved-base absence remains unverified because Git metadata is unavailable. Require the approved-base check above before creation.
- Reuse existing tests/fixtures unchanged: harness workflow parsers and permission loader, validator trusted-policy/tamper fixtures, CLI authoritative-grant fixtures. No test additions or assertion weakening.
- Focused verification commands and role allocation are in TEST_PLAN.md. Planner performs source inspection only; developer runs workflow checks; tester runs the focused security checks once and reviews evidence. Full suites are not repeated per role.
- Checked assumptions: actual workflow triggers, distribution list, security-test names and no benchmarks were verified by file inspection/search. Git base identity remains explicitly unverified in this snapshot.
- Reopen the plan if the fixed commands require product runtime changes, a framework, weaker policy/protected-path enforcement, altered scaffold defaults, removed security assertions, or release gating cannot bind to one immutable commit. Do not expand scope to repair transport or deliver other queued PRs.
- **What this change breaks:** `README.md:81` and Makefile check comment currently equate local full checks with PR CI; update their wording. Release reusable-call permissions are asserted by `internal/harness/workflow_permissions_test.go:140`; preserve compatibility. Security-step equality/order and grant arguments in `internal/harness/scaffold_test.go:1017` must stay unchanged. `docs/GITHUB.md:131` names the consumer scaffold check: preserve unchanged because scaffold behavior is out of scope. `.github/workflows/security.yml` and fork-operation admission assertions (`internal/fork/operations_test.go:15`) remain unchanged. Existing full-suite tests, runtime fast-pass semantics, scaffold templates and `.goreleaser.yaml` remain unchanged. Review renamed/removed CI job names against hosted required checks before merge.

Security profile ownership: the fixed core package command runs harness/validation policy tests once; the named CLI command covers authoritative grants; gitcredential/safefs run package-wide; the anchored agent/sandbox/fork lists above cover credential rejection, isolation/snapshot confinement, fail-closed behavior and coordinator admission. Preserve existing skip/fail semantics and assertions. Use this exact deduplicated profile in policy, fixture expectations and developer documentation.

# ISSUE-334 verification

Use existing tests and offline workflow inspection only. No new tests, benchmarks, performance experiments or per-role full-suite runs. The approved base's required checks remain mandatory for this bootstrap PR; coordinator validation executes them once without candidate overrides.

## Focused commands

Mandatory security/smoke commands, once on every PR (including docs-only):

```bash
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/cli -run '^Test(CLIRepoValidateHarnessGrantNeedsAuthoritativeState|RepoValidateGrantOnlyRunsNoChecks|RepoValidateGrantFileRechecked|RootDefaultEnvironment|RootInjectedEnvironment|ResolveBuildVersion|ResolveBuildVersionWithoutVCS)$' -count=1
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/gitcredential/... ./internal/safefs/... -count=1
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/agent -run '^Test(DefaultModeNeverRunsHostAgent|OperatorCannotWeakenApprovedIsolation|MockCannotBypassIsolation|IsolatedRunnerRejectsHostCredentialsAndUnrestrictedNetwork|NativeCodexRejectsPolicyOverrides|NativeIsolatedEffortAdmitsNoOtherArguments|IsolatedBackendIsExplicit|ConfiguredRunnerRejectsPublishingCredentialForwarding|RestrictedEnvRemovesPublishingCredentials|ConfiguredRunnerWithLookupRejectsCredentialNames|AdapterProcessHidesPublishingCredentials)$' -count=1
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/sandbox -run '^Test(WorkerArchiveRoundTripAndImport|WorkerImportRejectsConcurrentChanges|WorkerRejectsHostileArchives|WorkerInputRejectsLinksAndCancellation|WorkerRejectsUnpinnedImageAndDoesNotForwardCredentials|WorkerInputRejectsPortableAliases|WorkerEmptyEnvironmentNeverInherits|WorkerOCIMissingCapabilitiesFailClosed|DependencyCacheNoFallback|NativeCodexBoundary|ToolExecutorBoundary)$' -count=1
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/fork -run '^Test(GatewayDeadlineCancelsInFlightScan|GatewayIgnoresMismatchedOrEditedResults|ForkJSONRejectsTrailingMalformedData|ForkCoordinatorSecurityAndLifecycle|OperationListsStayInSync|ForkRequestRejectsCarryAuthority)$' -count=1
```

The fixed core commands run in every environment, alongside the mandatory commands:

```bash
go test -timeout=10m ./internal/validation/... ./internal/harness/... ./internal/coordination/... ./internal/lease/... ./internal/contract/...
go test -timeout=5m ./cmd/changelog ./internal/changelog
```

Retain all-source formatting, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `go tool staticcheck ./...`. This identical fixed profile covers ordinary, protected/security, broad, unknown and docs-only changes. The CLI package runs only the named tests per PR; full CLI and repository suites run nightly/release. Inspect policy commands for absence of Git/diff selection, base/environment dependencies and candidate helpers. No selector failure cases remain.

For AC1/AC4, use two disposable repository fixtures with the revised fixed policy committed as their explicitly trusted base and the existing isolated/native configuration. Make an ordinary changelog-code change in one and a protected workflow/policy change in the other. Outside a CI runner (so `RunnerIsolated` cannot bypass native isolation), from each fixture run the existing `swarm repo validate --base "$FIXTURE_BASE" --protected-paths report` using the checkout's built CLI; the base is validator input, never command environment. This exercises the actual native validation runner, not a shell simulation. Record that check snapshots omit `.git` and the runner's cleaned environment contains no base variables, plus actual fixed-command results for both cases. Reuse only existing tests; add no test files or assertions. Report mode demonstrates protected edits without manufacturing a grant; existing grant/enforcement tests above retain rejection coverage. These disposable fixtures do not authorize the candidate policy for the real bootstrap PR. If native execution is unavailable, record the limitation for review; do not substitute a full Git checkout shell run or weaken isolation.

Use the same commands for implementation verification; record results once and reuse evidence across roles. Do not edit existing tests. Independently inspect protected-path list and token-bearing step equality against the approved base. Names were verified by source search. No timing probes or benchmark claims.

## Acceptance mapping

| Criterion | Evidence and verification |
| --- | --- |
| AC1: fast relevant regressions with trust/static/security preserved | Run focused commands above. Inspect YAML to confirm one owner for fmt/build/vet/staticcheck/tests, existing security.yml admission retained, trusted-base policy/grant flow unchanged, PR events in `swarm-validate.yml` have no repository-wide `go test` (including any flagged variant), no `-race`, no GOOS loop, no benchmarks and no call to `full-validation.yml`. Execute the ordinary and protected fixtures through actual isolated-native validation as specified above; both run the identical fixed commands without snapshot Git metadata or base environment. Reuse existing tamper and grant tests for authority cases. |
| AC2: nightly/manual full validation and results | Inspect full workflow schedule, workflow_dispatch and workflow_call admission, bounded jobs, immutable checkout, Ubuntu/bwrap setup, full normal/race commands, six Go OS/architecture pairs against .goreleaser.yaml, failure-preserving log capture, always-upload results and retention. Record benchmark search gap (no Benchmark functions or appropriate target); no new performance execution. Hosted run can confirm scheduling after merge; offline checks satisfy this WorkUnit's admission demonstration. |
| AC3: exact release commit full gate and shared definitions | Existing reusable-permissions test checks every local workflow call. Independently trace release event -> immutable SHA -> shared full workflow checkout -> eligibility -> snapshot/publish checkout/needs. Inspect failure/skipped full gate means publish cannot run, tag ancestry and environment checks remain, no secrets inherited into candidate testing and no stale nightly success reused. Inspect concurrency for caller/callee cancellation/deadlock and ensure PR never calls the full workflow. |
| AC4: demonstrations and assertions preserved | Retain actual isolated validation transcripts for ordinary and protected fixtures (identical mandatory and fixed core commands, no repository-wide test command), source workflow admission trace for schedule/manual/tag/snapshot, checked SHA and focused command outcomes in validation evidence. Confirm no existing test assertions were edited or removed, full suites remain in shared workflow, and no product/scaffold changes. The bootstrap coordinator's trusted full-policy result is separate from the future fast-lane demonstration. |

For edited workflows, use `actionlint` if already available; otherwise record its absence and inspect expressions, events, needs, permissions and reusable-call contracts explicitly. Extract each changed bash run block and check with `bash -n` after substituting Actions expressions with inert values; validate documented bash snippets similarly. Check relative documentation links and the changelog fragment. Do not install a new validation framework.

Nightly/release run the existing full commands, not each role:

```bash
go test -timeout=15m ./...
go test -race -timeout=15m ./...
for target in linux/amd64 linux/arm64 darwin/amd64 darwin/arm64 windows/amd64 windows/arm64; do
  GOOS=${target%/*} GOARCH=${target#*/} CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/swarm
done
```

Only implementation/CI runs these full checks as required; planning does not. Report unavailable hosted execution as a verification limit, never as a successful live run. Agent review remains independent and bound to the exact plan/test-plan artifacts.

Security profile ownership: the fixed core package command runs harness/validation policy tests once; the named CLI command covers authoritative grants; gitcredential/safefs run package-wide; the anchored agent/sandbox/fork lists above cover credential rejection, isolation/snapshot confinement, fail-closed behavior and coordinator admission. Preserve existing skip/fail semantics and assertions. Use this exact deduplicated profile in policy, fixture expectations and developer documentation.

VERDICT: APPROVED

Scope of this review (operator instruction): only the F1/F2 corrections (explicit existing security test lists and deduplication). The previously accepted design and scope are kept as they were. No new tests, probes or benchmarks were requested or run.

| Check | Result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F1: security lists name real tests | Pass | Each of the 34 anchored names (cli 7, agent 11, sandbox 11, fork 6) matches exactly one `func Test<Name>(` in its package. Files: `internal/cli/{repo_validate_grant,environment,version}_test.go`, `internal/agent/{isolation_policy,adapters}_test.go`, `internal/sandbox/{worker,worker_oci,dependency_cache,native,executor}_test.go`, `internal/fork/{transport_security,fork,operations,comment_format}_test.go`. None of these files has a restrictive build tag. |
| F1: whole-package security commands resolve | Pass | `go list ./internal/gitcredential/... ./internal/safefs/...` resolves to exactly those two packages, and both have test files. |
| F1: the profile has no selection logic | Pass | The commands are fixed, with no Git, diff, base or environment input. Anchored `^Test(...)$` patterns cannot pick up extra top-level tests by prefix (for example, `ResolveBuildVersion` and `ResolveBuildVersionWithoutVCS` are both listed explicitly). Subtests still run. |
| F2: no package runs twice | Pass | `go list` shows no overlap between the core set (validation, harness, coordination, lease, contract, cmd/changelog, internal/changelog) and the security set (cli, gitcredential, safefs, agent, sandbox, fork). The ownership paragraph matches this split. |
| F2: PLAN and TEST_PLAN agree | Pass | The `go test` profile lines in PLAN.md and TEST_PLAN.md are textually identical (diffed). TEST_PLAN additionally lists the nightly/release full commands, which is intended. |
| Prior accepted design preserved | Pass | No changes to trust-base policy, the protected-path list, release gating, the full-validation workflow, documentation, or the bootstrap rule. |

## Findings

None blocking.

Non-blocking note for the implementer: `-count=1` appears on the security commands but not on the core commands. This makes no difference in fresh CI/native snapshots, so the plan can stay as it is. Keep the profile text identical in the policy, the fixtures and `docs/developer.md`, as the plan requires.

## Operator guidance

> Review only the F1/F2 corrections: explicit existing security test lists and deduplication; preserve prior accepted design and scope. No new tests, probes or benchmarks.
